:::{#rem-matrix-induced-inner-product-bilinear}
#### A matrix-induced inner product is a symmetric bilinear form

When $\matr{A}$ is [symmetric](#def-symmetric-matrix) and [positive definite](#def-positive-definite),
its [matrix-induced inner product](#def-matrix-induced-inner-product)
is the same function as its [symmetric bilinear form](#def-symmetric-bilinear-form),
since both are defined as $\tp{\vx}\, \matr{A}\, \vy$:

$$
\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}} = \bform{\matr{A}}{\vx}{\vy}.
$$

A [symmetric matrix](#def-symmetric-matrix) that is not positive definite
still has a symmetric bilinear form,
but that form is not an [inner product](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-inner-product).
For example, take $\matr{B}$ from @exm-symmetric-bilinear-form
and the vector $\vecf{z} = \tp{(1, -1)}$:

$$
\ba
\bform{\matr{B}}{\vecf{z}}{\vecf{z}}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd (-1) \\ 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vecf{z} \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 1 \cd (-1) + (-1) \cd 1
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= -2.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

The [quadratic form](#def-quadratic-form) of $\matr{B}$ is negative at $\vecf{z}$,
so $\matr{B}$ is not positive definite.

:::
